meta.title: Ch 18: SDG & ESG Assurance (Emerging Areas) — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 18 (SDG & ESG Assurance (Emerging Areas)).

questions.q: A manufacturer's indirect GHG emissions from purchased electricity and from its suppliers' operations are:
questions.why: GHG Protocol: Scope 1 = owned sources (boilers, fleet); Scope 2 = purchased energy (the electricity line above); Scope 3 = the value chain, upstream AND downstream (supplier operations, transport, product use); the audit angle: allocation logic and completeness of Scope 3 are the usual misstatement zones.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — owned, bought, and everything else — the ladder of responsibility AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Scope is a map, not a fence.

questions.q: A sustainability data assurance engagement (ISAE/SAE-3000-type) providing 'nothing has come to our attention' is:
questions.why: Sustainability assurance uses the assurance stack (limited→negative, reasonable→positive) over the chosen criteria (GHG protocol, GRI/SASB/ESRS, BRSR in India); the practitioner evaluates subject-matter risk and evidence — for a first-time assurer, expect disclosure on the criteria's suitability and data lineage.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the assurance level is decided by the wording, not the topic AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A new domain keeps the old ladder of caution.

questions.q: For Indian listed entities' BRSR sustainability reporting, the audit-readiness point to verify is:
o: Phased assurance (type and coverage) is prescribed by the markets regulator for the listed universe — check the current SEBI circular for which sections and which assurance level apply in the exam year
questions.why: BRSR (structured: P1 principles, P2 processes, P9 KPI metrics incl. GHG, water, waste, social) replaced voluntary reporting for the top listed entities with assurance phasing introduced via amendment; the DANGEROUS detail (which entities/which level/when) is exactly the amendment-verification item.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — regulatory phasing moves — verify the date before you cite the %, do cite the structure AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Readiness is not compliance, but it audits the same way.

questions.q: Which is a Scope 2 emission for a factory?
questions.why: Scope 2 = purchased energy (electricity/heat/steam); fleet is 1; commuting and investments are 3.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — owned, bought, others AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Meter your own, own what you buy, borrow the rest.

o: A negative conclusion — nothing has come to the practitioner's attention
questions.why: Same ladder as financial reviews: limited→'nothing came to attention'; reasonable→positive wording on the subject against criteria.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the phrasing is the level AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: SEBI's sustainability reporting regime (BRSR) and its assurance provisions — the exam-safe handling is:
o: State the BRSR structure (principles, processes, disclosures incl. GHG scope 1/2/3, water, waste, social capital) and say the assurance scope/level/coverage must be verified against the CURRENT circular for the attempt year
questions.why: MOVING TARGET: the phasing of assurance type and coverage has been amended in stages; the documented answer is structure + 'verify the notification', never a hard-coded year in the body of the answer.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — structure is stable, the calendar isn't AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Assurance phasing moves — cite the framework, verify the date.

questions.q: BRSR Core/metric-level expectations push assurance focus for GHG data onto:
o: Boundary completeness (operational control vs equity share), emission-factor sourcing, and restatement policy for method changes — the numbers' lineage
questions.why: The reporting standards' shift from prose to metric sets (and limited assurance of select KPIs) moves the practitioner's risk assessment exactly where data integrity is manufactured: boundaries, factors, restatements.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — lineage over layout AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Carbon numbers have plumbing; assurance inspects it.

questions.q: In an ESG assurance engagement, the practitioner's threshold question before any fieldwork is:
o: Whether the criteria (reporting framework, boundaries, metrics definitions) are suitable and available — without firm criteria, data cannot be 'wrong', only differently framed
questions.why: Suitability and availability of criteria decide assurance itself: completeness boundaries (sites, JV scope), metric definitions (GHG protocol scopes, intensity denominators), restatement policies — a framework named but not consistently applied collapses to a disclaimer or qualified conclusion.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — define 'true' before testing it AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: You cannot audit a footprint if nobody drew the yard.

questions.q: A limited-assurance ESG report expresses its conclusion as:
o: Positive assurance: 'in our opinion the report is prepared in all material respects...'
Negative assurance: 'nothing has come to our attention causing us to believe it is materially misstated'
questions.why: The wording mirrors financial audit practice: reasonable assurance = positive opinion, limited = 'nothing came to our attention'; limited work (analytical, inquiry, some testing) reduces risk to an acceptable-but-higher level than an audit's — the conclusion style is the tell of the engagement's depth.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the grammar of doubt vs the grammar of conviction AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A negative-assurance sentence is a fence with a low bar, not a wall.

questions.q: Scope 1 emissions of a newly acquired plant should be:
o: Included from the acquisition date under the consolidation/boundary approach the entity adopts consistently (equity vs operational control) — and the change is disclosed as a restatement policy application
questions.why: GHG accounting inherits the consolidation logic: the boundary method (operational control usually in BRSR-land) decides inclusion, and mid-year events start on the event date; the comparability discipline = disclosure of the method and its changes.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the carbon balance sheet keeps the same consolidation diary AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: New factory, new emissions — from the day you run it.

questions.q: In a sustainability data assurance engagement, the practitioner's interest in the client's data controls exists because:
o: Weak controls (no sign-off on emissions factors, no reconciliation of utility bills to sites) cap the assurance LEVEL regardless of substantive re-performance
They are the FS auditor's job exclusively
questions.why: ESG data lineage is thin: the practitioner cannot reasonable-assure a spreadsheet culture; where controls can't carry reliance, the ceiling is limited assurance — the level choice IS a controls assessment.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the level is bought with controls, not years Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.
